**Dutch banks and PSPs agree roadmap for next phase of iDEAL-to-Wero migration**

*EPI, major Dutch banks and nine payment service providers have committed to a joint roadmap for the next stage of migrating iDEAL transactions to Wero, a critical test of whether EPI can consolidate national payment schemes at scale.*

The European Payments Initiative has announced that ABN Amro, ING, Rabobank and Dutch payment service providers such as Adyen, Mollie, Buckaroo, CM.com and MultiSafepay have agreed the roadmap for the next major phase of migrating iDEAL to Wero. The announcement follows what EPI described as a successful first step in the transition.

The Netherlands is a pivotal market for EPI's ambitions. iDEAL dominates Dutch e-commerce with deep consumer and merchant adoption, making a smooth migration essential both operationally and symbolically. Bringing nine acquirers and payment service providers into the agreed roadmap — rather than relying solely on banks — signals that EPI is treating merchant-side infrastructure as a first-order concern, not an afterthought.

The joint commitment does not yet specify a completion date, but the breadth of participants suggests EPI is moving past early pilot stages toward a structured, market-wide rollout. How quickly Dutch consumers and merchants experience the switch will set expectations for Wero's ability to absorb national schemes elsewhere.

*Sources: [EPI embarks on next phase of iDeal transition to Wero](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110453/epi-embarks-on-next-phase-of-ideal-transition-to-wero?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Montenegro launches instant payments aligned with SEPA standards**

*Montenegro's instant payments system went live on July 20, making it the latest non-EU country to adopt SEPA-aligned infrastructure and extending Europe's real-time settlement footprint.*

Montenegro's central bank launched domestic instant payments on July 20, enabling transfers that settle in seconds between citizens and businesses. The system has been built to comply with European standards, consistent with the country's EU accession trajectory.

The Association of Banks of Montenegro confirmed that instant payments are now available in real time, with director Marija Šuković framing the launch as alignment with "the highest European standards." The World Bank's vice president for Europe attended the launch alongside Montenegro's minister of European affairs, underscoring the geopolitical dimension of payments infrastructure convergence.

Montenegro joins a growing list of non-eurozone countries — including Iceland, which connected to TIPS in June — adopting euro-area instant payments standards. For banks and processors operating across south-east Europe, the launch creates new interoperability possibilities but also raises questions about how quickly cross-border connectivity will follow domestic go-live.

*Sources: [CBCG: Instant payments in Montenegro from today, money arrives in a few seconds](https://en.vijesti.me/news-b/economy-d/818514/cbcg-from-today-instant-payments-in-Montenegro-money-arrives-in-a-few-seconds) — Vijesti | [Association of Banks: Instant payments in the country in real time available to citizens and ...](https://en.vijesti.me/news-b/economy-d/818503/Association-of-banks-makes-instant-payments-in-the-country-available-to-citizens-and-businesses-in-real-time) — En*

**CFPB acting director signals forthcoming open banking rule at Senate hearing**

*The acting head of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau told senators that a new open banking proposal is coming, offering the first concrete indication of the agency's direction since it rewrote Section 1033 in June.*

The CFPB's acting director defended the agency's enforcement freeze at a Senate hearing and signalled that a fresh open banking proposal is forthcoming. The statement is the clearest indication yet of how the bureau intends to proceed after its June rewrite of the Section 1033 rule, which narrowed data scope and introduced fees for fintech access to consumer bank data.

The June revision drew sharp criticism from fintechs, who argued it would limit competition by allowing banks to charge for data access. A National Review commentary published alongside the hearing warned that the forthcoming rule risks enabling "data-rationing fees" that would undermine the original intent of open banking. The political fault lines are now clearly drawn: banks favour the narrower scope and fee structure, while fintechs and consumer advocates want broader, free access restored.

For European observers, the US trajectory offers a counterpoint. Where PSD2 and its successors established data access as a regulatory baseline, the US debate remains stuck on whether access should carry a price. The outcome will shape how US-headquartered fintechs with European operations allocate product investment between the two markets.

*Sources: [CFPB Chief Defends Enforcement Freeze](https://legis1.com/news/cfpb-enforcement-freeze-chief-defends-at-senate) — Legis1 | [Don't Let Banks Charge Data-Rationing Fees](https://www.nationalreview.com/2026/07/dont-let-banks-charge-data-rationing-fees/) — National Review*

**Abound and ClearScore partner to automate debt consolidation via open banking**

*ClearScore is integrating its automated debt repayment technology with Abound's open-banking-powered lending, illustrating how open banking data is moving beyond underwriting into active loan management.*

ClearScore, the credit marketplace, is partnering with Abound to scale debt consolidation loans that use open banking data both for credit assessment and for automating the repayment of existing debts. The integration means borrowers taking a consolidation loan through Abound can have their outstanding balances identified and settled automatically using ClearScore's repayment technology.

The partnership is notable less for its commercial terms than for what it represents structurally. Open banking's role in consumer lending has largely centred on affordability checks and income verification at the point of underwriting. Using the same data rails to manage post-origination cash flows — identifying creditors, calculating outstanding balances and initiating repayments — extends open banking deeper into the loan lifecycle.

For UK lenders watching open finance regulation take shape, this is an early example of the kind of multi-step, data-dependent product that the FCA's smart data framework is designed to enable. Whether it scales will depend on borrower willingness to grant the broader data permissions required.

*Sources: [Abound to Scale Debt Consolidation Loans with ClearScore's Automated Debt Repayment ...](https://financialit.net/news/lending/abound-scale-debt-consolidation-loans-clearscores-automated-debt-repayment-technology) — Financialit*
